answer: An agent marketplace selling tundra maps, canyon surveys, and quill designs assigns voting power by escrowed stake, not account count. Splitting one deposit among a thousand identities therefore adds no influence. Each vote signs a proposal hash; two conflicting votes for the same round provide public proof that triggers slashing. To gain control, an attacker must buy and lock enough stake to outweigh honest agents, risking its loss if caught double-signing.
